critical_code_review_comments: findCatDropTarget in TasksPanel.jsx uses document.elementsFromPoint(clientX, clientY) which correctly finds the underlying chip even when the framer-motion drag layer visually constrains the card to Y-axis — clean approach, confirmed working with real cursor coords.

persistCatOrder swallows the server error via .catch(() => {}) — localStorage still updates so UI stays consistent, but a silent server error would leave devices out of sync without any user feedback. Consider a toast on failure for cross-device correctness. Non-blocking.
handleTaskDropCategory early-returns when current === next — good idempotency guard preventing unnecessary PATCH calls.

context_for_next_testing_agent: To simulate the framer-motion task-drag-onto-chip: (1) query [data-testid=task-drag-{id}], (2) page.mouse.move to handle center, page.mouse.down, (3) small jiggle (~8 sub-pixel moves of ~2px each with 25ms waits) to let framer engage dragControls, (4) page.mouse.move(chip_center_x, chip_center_y, steps=35), (5) page.mouse.up. The chip gets ring-2 ring-sertex-cyan/80 while cursor hovers, and toast 'Görev → {name}' shows on drop. For chip-reorder use playwright's page.drag_and_drop (HTML5-dnd path). Token is stored in localStorage['sertex_token_v1']. Session invalidates on second login (single-session enforcement) — reuse the LS token for API verifications inside the same page context.
